title: Donors and acceptors shift carrier populations
caption: Doping changes silicon's electrical behavior by introducing controlled atoms into the lattice; chemical presence alone is not sufficient activation. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Donor doping
nodes.detail: Suitable impurities contribute mobile electrons.

nodes.label: Acceptor doping
nodes.detail: Suitable impurities increase the hole population.

nodes.label: Substitutional lattice sites
nodes.detail: Electrically useful dopants occupy appropriate crystal positions.

title: Heat spreads dopant from a surface source
caption: Diffusion creates a depth profile through thermally activated atomic movement; time and temperature couple dose distribution and junction depth. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Surface dopant supply
nodes.detail: A source establishes dopant at the wafer surface.

nodes.label: Thermal exposure
nodes.detail: Heating allows atoms to move through silicon.

nodes.label: Depth profile
nodes.detail: Concentration changes with distance from the surface.

nodes.label: Doped region
nodes.detail: The resulting profile affects the device's electrical behavior.

title: Select ions, set their energy, count their delivery
caption: An implanter separates species before delivering a controlled beam to the wafer; dose and energy serve different controls. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Ion source
nodes.detail: The source creates charged dopant species.

nodes.label: Mass analysis
nodes.detail: Magnetic selection separates the desired beam species.

nodes.label: Beam-energy control
nodes.detail: Acceleration or deceleration sets implantation energy.

nodes.label: Wafer exposure
nodes.detail: Beam current and scan control determine delivered dose.

title: One beamline cannot optimize every implant
caption: High current, high energy and precision dose control impose different engineering demands. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: High-current implant
nodes.detail: Beam delivery prioritizes large ion flux.

nodes.label: High-energy implant
nodes.detail: Acceleration enables deeper implantation.

nodes.label: Medium-current precision
nodes.detail: Selected applications favor tightly controlled beam quality and dose.

source.heading: 4. Implanter Classes, Tools and Special Modes

title: Ions stop through statistical collision histories
caption: Nuclear and electronic stopping contribute differently with ion species and energy; an implanted profile is a distribution, not a single depth. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Nuclear collisions
nodes.detail: Momentum transfer deflects ions and displaces silicon atoms.

nodes.label: Electronic stopping
nodes.detail: Energy transfers to the electronic system.

nodes.label: Range distribution
nodes.detail: Different trajectories finish at different depths.

nodes.label: Channeling paths
nodes.detail: Crystal alignment can let some ions travel farther.

source.heading: 5. Where the Ions Stop: Range Statistics

title: Implant damage changes the later anneal response
caption: A primary collision can launch a cascade; the resulting defects influence repair and dopant redistribution. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Incoming ion
nodes.detail: The projectile transfers energy to lattice atoms.

nodes.label: Collision cascade
nodes.detail: Displaced atoms trigger further local collisions.

nodes.label: Damaged or amorphous region
nodes.detail: Disorder accumulates in the implanted layer.

nodes.label: Anneal response
nodes.detail: Defect evolution affects activation and transient diffusion.

source.heading: 6. Damage, Amorphisation and Transient Enhanced Diffusion

title: Annealing balances repair against unwanted diffusion
caption: More thermal exposure can repair and activate the lattice while also spreading the dopant profile. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Lattice repair
nodes.detail: Heat helps restore crystalline order.

nodes.label: Electrical activation
nodes.detail: Dopants move into electrically useful sites.

nodes.label: Profile spreading
nodes.detail: Atomic motion can blur the intended junction.

nodes.label: Time-temperature choice
nodes.detail: The recipe balances the competing requirements.

title: Modern logic uses implants in several supporting roles
caption: Device architecture changes where implants are useful; in-situ doped epitaxy complements rather than simply duplicates beam implantation. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Wells and isolation
nodes.detail: Implants define selected substrate regions.

nodes.label: Device adjustments
nodes.detail: Selected implant steps tune electrical behavior.

nodes.label: Source/drain epitaxy
nodes.detail: Growth can introduce dopant during crystal formation.

nodes.label: Integrated transistor flow
nodes.detail: The process combines several methods of placing dopants.

source.heading: 8. Implants in a Modern FinFET and GAA Flow

title: Doping requirements extend beyond logic gates
caption: Image sensors, memory and power devices need different profiles because they collect, store or block charge differently. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Image-sensor photodiode
nodes.detail: A doped junction collects charge generated by light.

nodes.label: Memory structures
nodes.detail: Selected profiles support storage-device operation.

nodes.label: Power devices
nodes.detail: Depth and concentration shape voltage and current behavior.

title: Measure the chemical profile and the electrical result
caption: Dose monitoring, depth analysis and post-anneal electrical measurements answer different questions about the implant. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Fast process monitor
nodes.detail: Indirect signals reveal implant consistency.

nodes.label: Depth-profile analysis
nodes.detail: Destructive measurements locate dopant concentration with depth.

nodes.label: Electrical measurement
nodes.detail: Activated carriers determine the post-anneal response.

nodes.label: Qualified implant
nodes.detail: Combined evidence checks delivery and functional outcome.

title: Containment and interlocks interrupt distinct hazard paths
caption: Implant equipment combines toxic source materials, high voltage and radiation hazards; this is a conceptual protection map, not an operating procedure. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Gas containment
nodes.detail: Engineered enclosures and exhaust isolate hazardous source materials.

nodes.label: Electrical interlocks
nodes.detail: Controlled access limits exposure to energized equipment.

nodes.label: Radiation shielding
nodes.detail: Enclosures and monitoring address generated radiation.

nodes.label: Protected operation
nodes.detail: Qualified procedures and equipment safeguards work together.

title: Dose, beam current and handling jointly set throughput
caption: A stronger beam helps only within process and equipment limits; wafer exchange and qualification also consume time. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Available beam current
nodes.detail: Ion delivery rate constrains exposure time.

nodes.label: Required dose
nodes.detail: More ions per area require more delivery work.

nodes.label: Handling and setup
nodes.detail: Loading, tuning and recipe changes add non-exposure time.

nodes.label: Qualified output
nodes.detail: Useful throughput counts wafers meeting the implant requirements.
